questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I wanted to get a familiar relationsship to an European city, and I love Paris.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There were scheduled about two meetings which were okay but not super informative. Moreover, most of it was in French, and many students in the room didn't speak not understand French.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Stated above.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not that easy. Rules on renting are pretty strict in France, and rent is also super expensive if you want to live in a central spot.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Landlords requires to be presented by a lot of documents, and the housing is expensive in general. I ended up finding housing on Air Bnb, which I was very satisfied with, since I avoided the part with the many documents.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You wait to choose your courses until the very last minute which makes no sense. The time tables are also only available right before the classes begin, and many of the courses you want will often clash. This proces was very frustrating.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We went to the international office many times as well as every other exchange student. But they had too little staff to keep up, so we often waited for hours.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not succesful at all. I wanted English classes only, which was a possibility that the university wrote about on their website. But as soon as I saw the time tables, I realized that this would not be possible. After about two months of dealing with the issue, I gave up and ended up only achieving 26 ECTS points, since there were not enough courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't go to this university if you want English taught classes only and want to achieve 30 ECTS points.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All of the English classes were at BA-level. The courses were also small (4 ECTS points each) which made the course quite superficial. Also, when being on your masters, you have an advantage of having some knowledge of the different fields from finishing you bachelor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. Mostly big lectures, writing down everything the teacher says, and no books.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: French Constitutional Law, French Business Law, History of Codifications, Introduction to Crossborder Litigation, Law and Economics of the Firm, French Law of Obligations.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: French Constitutional Law because the teacher was really cool. French Law of Obligations because it felt somewhat relevant to get to know some of these general terms in English.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing I can recall.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping was just as expensive as in Denmark. Eating out is generally cheaper than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some sport activities (I didn't look into these) and very few social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't go to any activities planned by the universities. Only events I looked up for myself.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about visiting other cities! Paris is huge, and there're so many things to do.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took me some time to adjust the French way of dealing with administrative issues. They stick to the same rules always even if these rules makes no sense and/or are super ineffective.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The one stated above.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That it felt like everyone was out every night. All restaurants, cafes and bars were full on both week nights and in the weekend. It creating a very unique ambience.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Be prepared of the administrative chaos, 2) go out to eat as much as you can (!) but be aware of the very well-known, touristy places (these are good, but way more expensive than the local, authentic restaurants), and 3) be active in the search of other exchange students - the university was not helpful in this regard.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing I can recall.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting Paris as a second home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with the host university.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
